name: Asaiah
overview: Asaiah is a male individual identified in Scripture as a member of the tribe of Simeon. He is referenced specifically in 1 Chronicles 4:36, which highlights his Simeonite heritage. Beyond this tribal affiliation and gender, Scripture provides minimal additional detail about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Asaiah means 'YHWH has made,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in the Hebrew language. This proper name emphasizes God's active role in the life or identity of this person, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 4:36.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Asaiah as a descendant of Simeon, establishing his tribal lineage. No further familial relationships are documented beyond this connection in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Asaiah's significance in the biblical narrative lies primarily in his identification as a Simeonite, which situates him within the broader history and genealogy of Israel. His mention in 1 Chronicles 4:36 contributes to the record of the tribe of Simeon, underscoring the importance of genealogical accounts in preserving the heritage and identity of God's people. Though brief, his inclusion affirms the providential hand of God in the formation of the tribes of Israel, consistent with the meaning of his name.
